title: Dropbox access token placeholders, references, masks, a token response without the token and prose
summary: The documented Bearer <TOKEN> form, a bare scheme, an environment reference, a masked display, a response carrying expires_in with no access_token, and prose that names the member.
rationale: Dropbox writes the header as Bearer <TOKEN> (claim access-token-exists), which is a documented placeholder; a bare scheme, a reference or a mask carries no value, and a response without the access_token member holds only a lifetime. Dropbox's labelled response examples are not used as controls: whether the exact example strings were ever issued is unresolved (sibling dropbox-labelled-response-example-tokens), so their non-secret status is not asserted. Flagging the controls here would redact documentation a reader needs.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are the documented placeholder, a bare scheme, references, masks or non-token members, not credential values; that such forms are not values is a project decision. Dropbox documents the Bearer <TOKEN> header form (carrier existence only).

sources.supports: Authorized requests to the API should use an Authorization header with the value Bearer <TOKEN>, where <TOKEN> is an access token obtained through the OAuth flow.
The length of time in seconds that the access token will be valid for.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
